positions.title: Independent Graphic Designer and Web Developer
positions.locationName: Brooklyn, New York, United States · Hybrid
positions.description:
Graphic designer and web developer in leading concept-driven, research-based, and technology-based projects. Specialized in developing visual systems across a wide range of design surfaces for various media and scales. 

Selected clients: Letterform Archive, MIT Press, NewLab,  Occupant Fonts, RISD Museum, Seoul Design Support Center, and UC Berkeley.

positions.title: Coordinator, Computation Technology and Culture (CTC)
positions.description: Coordinator for RISD’s interdisciplinary CTC concentration, which explores computation, critical theory, and creative practice. I advise students, recruit faculty, and support curriculum development across courses that integrate programming, software systems, and cultural inquiry.

positions.title: Assistant Professor, Graphic Design
positions.description: Full-time term appointment for the 19–22 academic years; teaching Graphic Design courses including Design Studio, Typography III, and electives for both graduate and undergraduate students on generative design and creative coding.

positions.locationName: New York, New York, United States

Work includes the creation of visual designs for interactive articles, infographics, and motion graphics, effectively communicating complex technical concepts to broad audiences.

positions.title: Co-Founder
positions.description:
KimChangPractice!! is a Seoul-based art collective comprised of an artist and a curator, focusing on the temporality of urban spaces and the networks behind the scenes. The group challenges conventional narratives and inspires new ways of addressing political issues through art. Spotlighted for defining a new generational vocabulary to engage with socio-political topics, their work spans exhibitions, publications, and workshops, fostering critical dialogues and exploring the intersections of art and activism. 
Exhibitions include the International Women Art Biennale (Incheon Art Platform, 2007), Life, No Peace, Only Adventures (Busan Museum of Art, 2011), The Republic of Two (Arko Art Center, 2013), and Wings of an Elephant: Future Project based on Fifteen Years of Social Art (Culture Station Seoul, 2013). These projects address themes such as urban soundscapes, collective memory, and the socio-political dynamics of urban development.
Featured in media outlets like Monthly Art Magazine and Hangyore Newspaper, KimChangPractice!! has received grants from the Incheon and Seoul Foundations for Arts and Culture. Their works are also included in collections at institutions such as the Wumin Art Center and Imsi Space.

positions.title: Product Designer
positions.description: A startup dedicated to creating office-based social networking services. Responsibilities included UI/UX design for web and mobile applications. Clients include KT Corporation.

positions.title: Web Designer & Database Administration Manager
positions.description: Managed databases and designed websites and web-based campaigns for governmental organizations. Clients included the Korea National Emergency Management Agency, the Korea Ministry of Public Safety and Security, and the United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction.

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description: Assisted Juyeon Cho—art theorist and translator of the Korean edition of The Return of the Real by Hal Foster—in editing the revised edition for its second printing. Additionally, served as a teaching assistant for a three-month class led by Juyeon Cho at Art Space Pool, focusing on reviewing and discussing the book.

positions.title: Curatorial Assistant
positions.description: A nonprofit art organization dedicated to initiating contemporary art productions and research aimed at fostering social, cultural, and political dialogue. Oversaw curatorial projects, research labs, workshops, and seminars featuring a diverse roster of invited guests, including artists, designers, historians, and sociologists.
